narrative.overview:
The category standard, executed at Vercel/Linear craft. A near-black ground holds one-step-lighter panels drawn by hairline borders, with high-contrast off-white text, one quieter secondary grey and one faint grey. A single indigo accent marks primary actions, focus and selection; green, amber and red speak only about state. Nothing is themed or metaphorical: the conventions (sidebar, summary tiles, tables, dialogs) are the commitment, and the quality lives in the details: even spacing on a 4px grid, compact 32px controls, tabular numerals, and machine literals set in mono.

The panel is dense but calm. Every page opens with a title and a one-line plain-Portuguese description, and unfamiliar rclone terms carry an inline "?" hint right where they appear. Live data (progress, quotas, counts) updates in place without shifting layout. A light theme exists as a full re-mapping of the same tokens under `:root[data-theme="light"]`; components never branch on theme.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default; light theme by token swap only.
Flat tonal layering with 1px hairlines; shadow only on floating layers.
One indigo accent; state colors carry meaning, never decoration.
Geist for UI, Geist Mono for machine literals; tabular numerals for every changing number.
Compact 32px control height, 6px control radius, 10px container radius.
Inline plain-language hints next to jargon.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Indigo is the only non-state hue. It means "act here", "you are here" or "this is selected"; it never decorates.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red appear only when they report a state (job status, quota level, connection, destructive consequence). Each comes as a solid ink plus a soft fill; pills and callouts use the soft fill with the solid ink.

rules.name: The Token-Swap Theme Rule
rules.body: Theme changes happen only by re-mapping tokens on the root. Components reference `var(--…)` and never hard-code a theme-specific value.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes or is compared (tile values, sizes, speeds, percentages, preview counts) uses tabular numerals so live updates never jitter.

rules.name: The Machine-Literal Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono marks text the machine reads: paths, remote names and `remote:path` routes, backend types, config keys, filter patterns and rate values. Prose, labels and numbers in sentences stay in Geist.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase, no tracked-out labels. Hierarchy comes from weight (400/500/600), size and the three ink levels.

rules.name: The Stable Row Rule
rules.body: Rows that hold live data keep one height whatever their state. Job rows fix their padding and give the progress cell a fixed width (260px) and a 36px minimum height, so progress, errors and "concluded" text swap without moving the table.

rules.name: The Hairline-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Anything resting on the page (panels, tiles, cards, tables) separates by border and tone. A shadow means "this floats and will go away".

dos: Do give every page a title and a one-line description, and attach a "?" hint to every rclone term where it first appears.
Do keep controls at 32px (28px for small) and on the 4px spacing scale.
Do set paths, remote names, `remote:path` routes and other machine literals in Geist Mono, and every changing number in tabular numerals.
Do reserve the indigo accent for the primary action, focus, selection and progress.
Do separate resting surfaces with 1px hairlines and tonal steps; use the Pop shadow only for floating layers.
Do style through tokens so the light theme follows automatically.
Do keep live rows a fixed height so progress updates never shift layout.
donts: Don't use green, amber or red for anything except state.
Don't add drop shadows to panels, tiles, cards or tables.
Don't introduce uppercase labels, tracked-out kickers or eyebrows above titles.
Don't set prose or UI labels in mono.
Don't add a second accent hue or gradients.
Don't hard-code colors in components; the hard-coded `#fff` on the danger button (about 3.2:1 on dark-theme red, below AA) is a known defect, not a pattern.
